name: The travel canon
note: An entry the canon admitted: two independent sources named it, the compiler's own list (written before anything was read) counting as one, the others editorial selections read on 2026-10-24 — travel publishers' and guides' lists of the kind's famous places by kind, category or city, and for a kind of work its famous works and museums' highlights, in several languages, each site read only as docs/sources/site-access.md allows. Which sources named each entry is kept under docs/local/research/calibration/, a guide's selection being its publisher's. Nothing was chosen or left out by Wikidata's classes, Wikipedia editions, readership or Wikivoyage's use of an item.

name: The American Society of Civil Engineers' Seven Wonders of the Modern World
note: As Wikipedia lists them. Its bridges, tunnels, dams and sea works name entries of Bridges & engineering marvels; the Panama Canal waits, with every canal, for the long-object model (#1948), and #1947 takes canals out of the kind's definition and its run; the CN Tower and the Empire State Building are not of that kind.

name: The BBC's Seven Wonders of the Industrial World
note: As Wikipedia lists them. The Brooklyn Bridge and the Hoover Dam are of Bridges & engineering marvels; the Panama Canal waits, with every canal, for the long-object model (#1948), and #1947 takes canals out of the kind's definition and its run; the SS Great Eastern, the Bell Rock Lighthouse, London's sewerage and the First Transcontinental Railroad are not.

name: Seven Wonders of the Waterways (Robert Aickman, Inland Waterways Association, 1946)
note: Membership read on the Wikipedia article about the list. Pontcysyllte Aqueduct, Barton Swing Aqueduct, Standedge Tunnel and Burnley Embankment left aside here: aqueducts, a tunnel and an embankment, not locks or lifts.

name: UNESCO World Heritage List
note: The property pages answer 403 to the fetch tool; membership taken from the title of the result on whc.unesco.org itself. Only property 856, The Four Lifts on the Canal du Centre, is a lock or lift; the Rideau Canal, the Canal du Midi and the Pontcysyllte Aqueduct and Canal are whole canals or an aqueduct and are left aside.

name: ASME Historic Mechanical Engineering Landmarks
note: Only landmark 205, the Peterborough Hydraulic (Canal) Lift Lock, is a lock or lift. The Morris Canal reaction turbine and the Chesapeake & Delaware scoop wheel are machinery, not places a boat climbs.

name: ASCE Historic Civil Engineering Landmarks
note: Locks and lifts on it: Hiram M. Chittenden Locks, the Morris Canal inclined planes, Davis Island Lock and Dam, Louisville and Portland Canal Locks & Dam, the Waterford Flight of Five. Whole canals (Panama, Suez, Erie, Göta, Canal du Midi, Caledonian and others) left aside: the kind's lock entries are one stop, not a canal.

name: The International Canal Monuments List (S. Hughes, ICOMOS/TICCIH, 1996)
note: Counted only the numbered sites under lock staircases, inclined planes and boat lifts; a lock named only in the prose is not counted. Whole canals, aqueducts, tunnels, dams, reservoirs and warehouses on the list are left aside. It predates 1996, so no later lift (Falkirk Wheel, Strépy-Thieu, Three Gorges) can be on it.
